title: NAD+ and Longevity: What the Science Says and What to Expect in Brisbane
html:
What Is NAD+ and Why Does It Decline With Age?

Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) is a coenzyme found in every cell of the human body. It plays a central role in energy metabolism, DNA repair, gene expression, and the regulation of cellular stress responses. Without adequate NAD+, cells cannot produce energy efficiently, repair damaged DNA, or maintain the signalling pathways that keep tissues healthy.

The problem is that NAD+ levels decline significantly with age. Research suggests that by the time we reach our 50s, NAD+ levels may be less than half of what they were in our 20s. This decline is associated with many of the hallmarks of ageing – reduced energy, slower recovery, cognitive changes, and increased susceptibility to age-related conditions.

At Australian Longevity Clinic Brisbane, we offer NAD+ infusion therapy as part of a personalised longevity and wellness program, assessed and supervised by our registered medical practitioners.

The Science Behind NAD+ and Ageing

NAD+ is the essential fuel for a group of proteins called sirtuins – often referred to as the body's "longevity genes." Sirtuins regulate inflammation, mitochondrial function, DNA repair, and cellular survival pathways. When NAD+ levels are sufficient, sirtuins function optimally. When NAD+ declines, sirtuin activity drops, and the cellular processes they regulate begin to deteriorate.

NAD+ is also required for the activity of PARP enzymes, which detect and repair DNA strand breaks. As we age and accumulate more DNA damage from environmental stressors, PARP enzymes consume increasing amounts of NAD+, further depleting the pool available for energy production and other vital functions.

Research into NAD+ precursors and direct NAD+ supplementation has grown substantially over the past decade, with studies examining its potential role in supporting metabolic health, neurological function, cardiovascular health, and overall cellular resilience.

What Are the Potential Benefits of NAD+ Therapy?

Patients who undergo NAD+ infusion therapy commonly report improvements across several areas of wellbeing. It is important to note that individual responses vary, and all treatments at Australian Longevity Clinic are individually assessed.

Energy and Mental Clarity NAD+ is directly involved in mitochondrial energy production. Individual responses to NAD+ therapy vary and are not guaranteed.

Recovery and Physical Performance NAD+ supports muscle cell repair and mitochondrial function, which are both critical for physical recovery. Athletes and active individuals often incorporate NAD+ therapy into their recovery protocols.

Sleep Quality NAD+ plays a role in circadian rhythm regulation. Individual responses vary.

Mood and Neurological Support NAD+ is a precursor to neurotransmitter synthesis pathways and supports neuronal energy metabolism. Emerging research is examining its potential role in supporting mood regulation and neurological resilience.

Cellular Longevity By supporting sirtuin activity and DNA repair mechanisms, NAD+ therapy is considered a foundational component of a comprehensive longevity medicine approach.

NAD+ Infusion vs. Oral Supplements: What Is the Difference?

Oral NAD+ precursors such as NMN (nicotinamide mononucleotide) and NR (nicotinamide riboside) are widely available and can support NAD+ levels over time. However, intravenous NAD+ infusion delivers the molecule directly into the bloodstream, bypassing the digestive tract and achieving significantly higher plasma concentrations than oral supplementation.

For patients where IV delivery is clinically indicated, your doctor will discuss the most appropriate approach based on your individual circumstances.

What to Expect From NAD+ Infusion Therapy in Brisbane

At Australian Longevity Clinic, NAD+ infusion therapy begins with a comprehensive medical consultation. Our doctors will review your health history, current symptoms, and wellness goals to determine whether NAD+ therapy is appropriate for you and to design a personalised protocol.

NAD+ infusions are typically administered over 1.5 to 3 hours, as the infusion rate must be carefully controlled to minimise side effects. Some patients experience mild sensations during the infusion – such as a feeling of warmth, chest tightness, or nausea – which resolve when the infusion rate is slowed. Our medical team monitors all patients throughout the procedure.

A typical initial course consists of 3 to 5 infusions over one to two weeks, followed by maintenance infusions as recommended by your treating doctor.

Who Is NAD+ Therapy Suitable For?

NAD+ infusion therapy may be appropriate for individuals who are experiencing:

  • Persistent fatigue or low energy that has not responded to other interventions
  • Cognitive changes associated with ageing or chronic stress
  • Reduced physical performance or slow recovery from exercise
  • A proactive interest in longevity medicine and cellular health optimisation
  • Neurodegenerative conditions (assessed on an individual basis)

NAD+ therapy is not suitable for everyone. Patients with certain medical conditions, including active cancer, pregnancy, or specific cardiovascular conditions, may not be appropriate candidates. A thorough medical assessment is always required before treatment.
